E003.note: n, K and the interval method are not stated in E003; values are sweeps.

E004.note: No measured noise exists for U; noise is swept and the break-even is reported.

gate_table.estimator: two one-sided tests per metric, paired by seed, 5% family-wise; number of metrics not stated
gate_table.gate: every primary quality metric: 90% CI of defended-minus-clean inside +-0.2 clean SD
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: Needs roughly 10-40+ paired runs depending on how exactly the defense reproduces the clean path. Measured recovery policies shift final NLL by 0.10-0.98 clean SD, so the 0.2 SD margin is met only by exact-semantics defenses.
gate_table.planned_n: not stated (promises 90% power from calibration, gives no number)

gate_table.estimator: observed fraction (no interval); 'corresponding' region not defined
gate_table.gate: >= 95% of defended runs finish inside the per-run +-0.2 SD region
gate_table.label: arithmetically impossible if the region is centred on the clean mean (unpaired); needs paired offset SD <= 0.102 clean SD if paired
gate_table.note: A clean run varies by 1 SD between seeds, so only 15.9% of runs can sit inside +-0.2 SD of a fixed centre even if the defense changes nothing. Pairing by seed fixes this, but only for defenses that reproduce the clean trajectory almost exactly. SC1 measured exact sync vs exact forward recovery equal to all digits, so exactness is reachable for those arms.

gate_table.estimator: '95% confidence bound' (method not stated); exact Clopper-Pearson one-sided assumed, two-sided and Wilson reported
gate_table.gate: lower 95% bound on critical-event interception >= 99%
gate_table.label: arithmetically impossible at n=100
gate_table.note: With 100 events the best possible bound is 0.05^(1/100)=0.970. At 299+ events a single miss fails the gate. For 80% power at n=300 the true miss rate must be about 0.05%, 20x lower than the claimed 1%. If the gate applies per family with F families, power is power^F.

gate_table.estimator: upper 95% bound; steps assumed independent (they are clustered by run)
gate_table.gate: upper 95% bound on false action per clean optimizer step <= 1%
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: A 1% ceiling is easy to resolve with tens of thousands of clean steps if steps are independent. They are not; the effective n is the number of runs.

gate_table.gate: clean time-to-target tax and facility-energy tax, upper 95% bound <= 2%
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: With the per-pair energy-ratio SD measured on this stack (3.6% with the cumulative counter) and 6 pairs, a true 0% tax passes only about a third of the time. About 17+ pairs are needed for 80% power at true tax 0, many more at 1%.

gate_table.gate: time and energy tax <= 2% at measured production fault incidence
gate_table.label: not evaluable (structural)
gate_table.note: The protocol itself says this is unevaluable until incidence is measured. Not a power question.
gate_table.planned_n: requires a fleet incidence measurement that does not exist

gate_table.estimator: paired 95% interval on an accounting ratio
gate_table.gate: redundant FLOPs <= 50% of uniform duplicate execution at the same protection level
gate_table.label: reasonable (accounting identity, little noise)
gate_table.note: FLOP counts are exact in the engine. Adequacy depends on how the protection level is matched, not on n.

gate_table.gate: falsified if any baseline matches the joint policy within uncertainty on all primary outcomes
gate_table.label: too lax
gate_table.note: Surviving only requires the CI to exclude 0 on at least one of K outcomes, in either direction. An identical baseline is 'not matched' with probability 1-0.95^K by chance; a baseline that is clearly better on one outcome also counts as not matching.

gate_table.estimator: machine-readable falsifier tests a point estimate; markdown says 'survive uncertainty analysis'
gate_table.gate: joint improves U >= 20% over best static
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: No noise measurement for U exists. Adequate (80% power at 1.25x claim, false pass <= 10%) only if the standard error of the gain is below the stated se; this needs the cluster-level SD of the paired gain to be frozen from calibration.
gate_table.planned_n: 30 seeds per cell; resampling unit = trace-day and failure domain (count not stated)

gate_table.estimator: machine-readable falsifier tests a point estimate; markdown says 'survive uncertainty analysis'
gate_table.gate: joint improves U >= 10% over independent-controller ensemble
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: No noise measurement for U exists. Adequate (80% power at 1.25x claim, false pass <= 10%) only if the standard error of the gain is below the stated se; this needs the cluster-level SD of the paired gain to be frozen from calibration.
gate_table.planned_n: 30 seeds per cell; resampling unit = trace-day and failure domain (count not stated)

gate_table.estimator: percentile cluster bootstrap on a contrast of 8 cell means
gate_table.gate: three-way interaction I_ABC >= 0.05 and cluster-bootstrap lower 95% bound > 0
gate_table.label: marginal
gate_table.note: The contrast adds 8 noisy cells with unit weight, so its SE is sqrt(8) times a cell's SE. Label is for 30 clusters and 5% per-cell CV with independent cells; labels change with noise and pairing, see key.
gate_table.planned_n: clusters not stated (>= 8 failure domains for the live claim)

gate_table.gate: regime crossing in >= 3 of 4 families; no static regime holds >= 90% of request-time in >= 2 families
gate_table.label: reasonable but not a test of benefit
gate_table.note: A controller that toggles regimes for no benefit satisfies it. It needs the utility gates beside it, which E004 does state.

gate_table.estimator: worst of F families; point vs interval not stated
gate_table.gate: no workload family loses > 1% utility or > 1 pp SLO attainment
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: Taking the worst of four noisy family estimates is a max over noise. With a 1% margin the per-family SE must be <= ~0.6% (point rule) or ~0.3% (interval rule).

gate_table.gate: nominal-90% intervals cover >= 80% of held-out outcomes
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: With 20 outcomes, a model whose true coverage is 70% passes about 11% of the time; with >= 50 outcomes it is controlled.
gate_table.planned_n: number of held-out outcomes not stated

gate_table.estimator: regret fraction; no threshold for ranking
gate_table.gate: intervention regret <= 10% of oracle value; held-out ranking 'fails'
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: The machine-readable protocol says no correlation threshold is set. 'Ranking fails' therefore cannot be decided.

gate_table.gate: CE improves >= 25% over best homogeneous co-design
gate_table.label: reasonable (point rule, n=2, noise=3.6%)
gate_table.note: Reading it as a point estimate is adequate at the measured noise. Reading it as a lower 95% bound with 2 runs per arm (t with 2 df) needs a much larger true gain. Noise anchors are an energy ratio and a loss, not CE itself.
gate_table.planned_n: 5 seeds/proxy candidate; >= 3 at 7-30B; >= 2 at target scale

gate_table.estimator: worst of F families; point vs interval not stated
gate_table.gate: no task-family metric regresses > 2% versus best homogeneous design
gate_table.label: requires implausible effect
gate_table.note: Even with zero true regression, requiring every one of F noisy metrics to clear 2% passes rarely under the interval reading, and only about half the time under the point reading when per-metric noise is 3% with 2 runs.

gate_table.gate: architecture-attributable share of the joint CE gain >= 50%
gate_table.label: reasonable
gate_table.note: Planted joint gain 25%. A ratio of two noisy differences is volatile when n is 2-3.

gate_table.estimator: point estimate of tau; regret of the argmax
gate_table.gate: held-out Kendall tau >= 0.70 and selected design within 10% of best observed CE
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: When seed noise equals the spread of true CE across candidates, even a perfect model cannot reach tau 0.7 reliably. The protocol must freeze the spread-to-noise ratio of the candidate set.
gate_table.planned_n: number of held-out candidates not stated
spec_gaps: spread of true CE across designs relative to seed noise

gate_table.gate: nominal-90% intervals have 85-95% empirical coverage
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: A perfectly calibrated model passes only when m is large. Check the 0.9 column.
gate_table.planned_n: number of held-out outcomes not stated

gate_table.gate: search energy <= 25% of one target-scale run
gate_table.label: reasonable at 1B proxies, binding at 7B+
gate_table.note: inferred: training FLOPs = 6*N*D with D = 20*N, so energy per run scales as N^2; 5 seeds per candidate; target N=70e9

gate_table.gate: >= 2 hardware classes deliver >= 20% of training FLOPs each
gate_table.label: reasonable (accounting)
gate_table.note: Deterministic accounting; no sampling noise.

gate_table.estimator: campus-day clustered CI; method not stated; exact CP one-sided assumed
gate_table.gate: event-level lower 95% bound on delivery probability >= 99%
gate_table.label: requires implausible effect (n=300, iid)
gate_table.note: 299 zero-failure events are required. At 300 windows one failure fails the gate. 80% power needs true delivery about 99.95%. A single virtual cell of 30 seeds can never pass (max bound 0.905). Campus-day clustering shrinks the effective n further.
gate_table.planned_n: >= 300 non-overlapping live windows; 30 seeds per virtual cell

gate_table.estimator: largest bid whose delivery bound passes
gate_table.gate: R_firm >= 20% of load; joint R_firm >= 1.5x best isolated
gate_table.label: arithmetically impossible if the 300 windows are split across bid levels; possible only with ~300 per bid
gate_table.note: Testing 20% needs its own 299 clean windows. If four bids share 300 windows, each gets 75 and the best possible bound is 0.961. On the 4-point grid, a joint R_firm of 20% needs the isolated best at or below 10%.

gate_table.estimator: worst of 4 families x (TTFT, TPOT, utility); point vs interval not stated
gate_table.gate: TTFT and TPOT SLO attainment fall <= 1 pp, utility <= 1%, in every workload family
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: Twelve simultaneous per-family constraints; per-family SE must be small relative to the 1 pp / 1% margin.

gate_table.gate: 30-minute post-event peak <= matched baseline peak + 5%
gate_table.label: underspecified
gate_table.note: If it must hold for every event, the per-event exceedance probability must be below 0.07% for 80% pass chance at 300 events.

gate_table.gate: 90% of bid in 10 s; full bid held 900 s; P99 TTFT/TPOT within limits
gate_table.label: folded into delivery probability (see E006-G3)
gate_table.note: If these are part of the event success indicator they only lower the true delivery probability that G3 must show is >= 99.95%.

gate_table.estimator: percentile bootstrap of the median, 90% interval, 10,000 draws
gate_table.gate: upper 90% bound of adaptive-minus-fixed NLL <= 0.01
gate_table.label: reasonable
gate_table.note: NLL differences reproduced exactly across LC3 and PW2, so the 6-value spread is between-schedule heterogeneity, not seed noise.

gate_table.gate: upper 90% bound of adaptive/fixed device-energy ratio <= 1.05
gate_table.label: requires implausible effect (with the instantaneous-meter noise actually used)
gate_table.note: Under the noise of the meter LC3 used, a true ratio of 1.0 or 1.023 fails this gate most of the time: the 'falsified' verdict is not informative about the energy. PW2's reproduction of the same contrast measured 1.023.

gate_table.gate: lower 90% bound of 2x2 interaction > 0
gate_table.label: n/a (claim has no magnitude)
gate_table.note: Read the value at mean/SD = 0 as the false-positive rate of the gate.

gate_table.gate: upper 90% bound of adaptive-minus-periodic_local NLL <= 0.01
gate_table.label: requires implausible effect
gate_table.note: Between-family SD 0.024 is more than twice the margin; n=6 cannot show noninferiority within 0.01.

gate_table.gate: upper bound of adaptive/periodic_local payload ratio <= 0.20
gate_table.label: arithmetically impossible
gate_table.note: periodic_local is the sparsest of the four available actions (32 state merges vs 256 gradient exchanges = 0.375x sync). No mix of the four can go below 1.0x periodic_local. Even against sync the best possible is about 0.31x, above 0.20x.

gate_table.gate: upper bound of adaptive/periodic_local completion-time ratio <= 0.90
gate_table.label: arithmetically impossible with whole-policy choices; per-tick mixing unproven
gate_table.note: The best whole-policy schedule is no faster than periodic_local in 4 of 6 families, so the median floor is 0.99.

gate_table.estimator: percentile bootstrap of the median, n=4
gate_table.gate: upper bound of normalized regret to hindsight envelope <= 0.10
gate_table.label: marginal
gate_table.note: Regret is >= 0 by construction and the envelope contains the adaptive run itself.

gate_table.gate: attempted-FLOP saving median >= 3%, lower bound > 0
gate_table.label: degenerate (deterministic quantum)
gate_table.note: Savings are multiples of 16,384/540,672 = 3.03% set by the failure schedule. The 3% bar equals one replay window; it tests the schedule, not the policy.

gate_table.gate: adaptive median ticks to target < fixed
gate_table.label: degenerate in the realised data (both crossed at the first 32-tick observation)
gate_table.note: Observation grid of 32 ticks forces ties once the target is crossed at the first observation. Taken from the LC1 write-up; not simulated.

e005_search_energy_arithmetic.assumption: inferred: training FLOPs = 6*N*D with D = 20*N, so energy per run scales as N^2; 5 seeds per candidate; target N=70e9
